docs.title: Cantera Reactive Flows
docs.text:
H\(_2\)/air with Cantera (h2o2.yaml), from thermodynamics to flames. Each page is a rendered, executed notebook; the cards open the clean versions.

  • Part 1: Equilibrium

    Adiabatic flame temperature, preheat, pressure, radicals and thermal NO\(_x\).

  • Part 2: Diffusion flames

    Counterflow flames, \(T(Z)\) against scalar dissipation, extinction.

  • Part 3: Premixed flames

    Flame structure, transport models, \(S_L(\phi)\), \(\delta_L(\phi)\), pressure and preheat.

The unedited notebooks are under the Original tab: Part 1, Part 2, Part 3.

Rebuild with python build_docs.py && mkdocs serve.

import pandas as pd

docs.title: Task 1 — Equivalence Ratio Sweep
docs.text:
\(T_\mathrm{ad}\) for \(\phi \in [0.4, 3.0]\) at \(T_u = 300\) K, 1 atm.

eq.equilibrium_temperature(phi, fuel, T_u, p, mechanism, oxidizer) returns \(T_\mathrm{ad}\) (K) for one condition: set \(\phi\), set \((T_u, p)\), equilibrate("HP"). Defaults: H\(_2\), 300 K, 1 atm, h2o2.yaml, air.

Reference value: \(\approx 2382\) K.

T_ad_st = eq.equilibrium_temperature(1.0)
print(f"T_ad(phi = 1, T_u = 300 K, 1 atm) = {T_ad_st:.1f} K")
Output
T_ad(phi = 1, T_u = 300 K, 1 atm) = 2387.6 K

\(2387.6\) K, within \(0.2\,\%\) of the reference.

eq.equilibrium_states(phi, T_u, p, ...) equilibrates many conditions at once (inputs are broadcast) and returns a SolutionArray. eq.equilibrium_sweep(phi_range, ...) is the same but returns only \(T_\mathrm{ad}\).

eq.save_states(states, name) saves states to results/part1/raw/<name>.csv via to_pandas(); plots.save_figure(fig, name) saves PDF and JPEG.

plots.plot(x, y, xlabel, ylabel, figsize, legend=True, grid=True, labels=..., ax=..., vlines=..., hlines=...) draws one or several curves.

phi = np.linspace(0.4, 3.0, 261)
states_phi = eq.equilibrium_states(phi, T_u=300.0, p=ATM)
eq.save_states(states_phi, "task1_phi_sweep")

T_ad = states_phi.T
k_max = np.argmax(T_ad)

fig, ax = plots.plot(
    phi, T_ad, r"Equivalence ratio $\phi$", r"Adiabatic flame temperature $T_\mathrm{ad}$ (K)",
    labels=[r"$T_u = 300$ K, $p = 1$ atm"], markevery=10,
    vlines={1.0: r"stoichiometric, $\phi = 1$"},
    title=r"$T_\mathrm{ad}$ vs equivalence ratio, H$_2$/air",
)
ax.plot(phi[k_max], T_ad[k_max], "*", color="k", ms=12,
        label=rf"peak: {T_ad[k_max]:.0f} K at $\phi = {phi[k_max]:.2f}$")
ax.legend()
plots.save_figure(fig, "task1_Tad_vs_phi")
plt.show()

eq.linear_slope(x, y) gives a fitted slope; eq.crossings(x, y, level) finds where a curve crosses a level. The 1000 K crossings lie outside \([0.4, 3]\), so a wider sweep is used.

lean, rich = phi <= 0.9, phi >= 1.3
print(f"Peak            : T_ad = {T_ad[k_max]:.1f} K at phi = {phi[k_max]:.2f}")
print(f"Lean-side slope : {eq.linear_slope(phi[lean], T_ad[lean]):7.0f} K per unit phi  (0.4 <= phi <= 0.9)")
print(f"Rich-side slope : {eq.linear_slope(phi[rich], T_ad[rich]):7.0f} K per unit phi  (1.3 <= phi <= 3.0)")

phi_wide = np.geomspace(0.02, 30, 2000)
T_wide = eq.equilibrium_sweep(phi_wide)
phi_lean_1000, phi_rich_1000 = eq.crossings(phi_wide, T_wide, 1000.0)
print(f"T_ad < 1000 K   : phi < {phi_lean_1000:.2f} (lean)   and   phi > {phi_rich_1000:.1f} (rich)")
Output
Peak            : T_ad = 2403.0 K at phi = 1.06
Lean-side slope :    1760 K per unit phi  (0.4 <= phi <= 0.9)
Rich-side slope :    -327 K per unit phi  (1.3 <= phi <= 3.0)
T_ad < 1000 K   : phi < 0.23 (lean)   and   phi > 9.5 (rich)

fig, ax = plots.plot(
    phi_wide, T_wide, r"Equivalence ratio $\phi$", r"$T_\mathrm{ad}$ (K)", xscale="log",
    hlines={1000.0: r"$T_\mathrm{ad} = 1000$ K"},
    vlines=[phi_lean_1000, phi_rich_1000], markevery=100, legend=True,
    title=r"Wide $\phi$ range: where the flame becomes too cold",
)
plots.save_figure(fig, "task1_Tad_vs_phi_wide")
plt.show()

docs.title: Answers
docs.text:
• Peak: \(\approx 2403\) K at \(\phi \approx 1.06\), not at \(\phi = 1\). Slightly rich mixtures suppress dissociation (excess H\(_2\) shifts \(\mathrm{H_2O \rightleftharpoons H_2 + \tfrac{1}{2}O_2}\) back), and the excess H\(_2\) adds little heat capacity.
  • Steeper lean side: \(+1760\) K vs \(-330\) K per unit \(\phi\). Lean, every bit of fuel removed is lost heat release; rich, heat release is capped by O\(_2\) and the extra H\(_2\) is only a light diluent.
  • Below 1000 K: \(\phi < 0.23\) and \(\phi > 9.5\). Below roughly 1000 K a flame cannot sustain itself, so these points bracket the flammability limits (measured for H\(_2\)/air: about \(\phi = 0.1\)–\(7\)).

docs.title: Answers
docs.text:
• Slope: \(\approx 0.70\), \(0.46\), \(0.58\) at \(\phi = 0.7\), \(1.0\), \(1.3\); well below 1. The extra enthalpy goes partly into dissociation, and hot products have a higher \(c_p\) than cold reactants.
  • Dependence on \(\phi\): yes. The slope is lowest at \(\phi \approx 1\) (hottest flame, most dissociation) and approaches 1 for very lean or rich mixtures. Higher pressure raises it near \(\phi = 1\).
  • Gain at 600 K: \(\approx 144\) K at \(\phi = 1\), less than half of the 300 K added. It is larger away from stoichiometric: \(\approx 218\) K at \(\phi = 0.7\), \(\approx 185\) K at \(\phi = 1.3\). So lean and rich are not the same.

docs.text:
\(\phi = 1\), \(T_u = 300\) K, \(p\) from 1 to 20 atm. eq.equilibrium_state(phi, ...) returns the equilibrated cantera.Solution, so any property can be read.

gas_st = eq.equilibrium_state(1.0)
top = sorted(gas_st.mole_fraction_dict().items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])
print(f"T_ad = {gas_st.T:.1f} K at 1 atm\n")
print(pd.DataFrame(top, columns=["species", "X"]).to_string(index=False, float_format="%.3e"))
Output
T_ad = 2387.6 K at 1 atm

species         X
     N2 6.458e-01
    H2O 3.244e-01
     H2 1.457e-02
     OH 7.285e-03
     O2 5.609e-03
      H 1.811e-03
      O 6.074e-04
    HO2 1.257e-06

eq.equilibrium_sweep_p sweeps pressure; eq.mole_fractions(states, species) extracts species; eq.power_law_exponent(x, y) fits \(y \propto x^n\).

states_p = eq.equilibrium_states(1.0, T_u=300.0, p=p)
eq.save_states(states_p, "task3_p_sweep")

X = eq.mole_fractions(states_p, species)

docs.title: Le Chatelier's principle
docs.text:
OH, H and O come from dissociation reactions that increase the number of gas moles, e.g. \(\mathrm{H_2 ightleftharpoons 2H}\), \(\mathrm{H_2O ightleftharpoons H + OH}\). Higher pressure shifts them back toward fewer moles:

\[ K_p(T) = \prod_i X_i^{ u_i}\left( rac{p}{p^\circ} ight)^{\Delta u} \quad\Rightarrow\quad X_\mathrm{H} \propto p^{-1/2} ext{ for } \mathrm{H_2 ightleftharpoons 2H} \] Symbol Meaning SI unit \(K_p\) Equilibrium constant – \(X_i\), \( u_i\) Mole fraction, stoichiometric coefficient – \(\Delta u\) Change in gas moles – \(p\), \(p^\circ\) Pressure, standard pressure Pa

docs.title: Thermal NO\(_x\)
docs.text:
Thermal NO is driven by O atoms (Zeldovich): \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d[NO]}}{\mathrm{d}t} \approx 2k_1[\mathrm{O}][\mathrm{N_2}]\), \(k_1 = 1.8\times10^{11}\, e^{-38370/T}\).

Symbol Meaning SI unit \([\cdot]\) Molar concentration kmol/m³ \(k_1\) Rate constant of \(\mathrm{O + N_2 \rightarrow NO + N}\) m³/(kmol·s) \(T\) Temperature K

eq.zeldovich_no_rate(states) evaluates this in ppm/ms. Gas-turbine conditions: \(T_u = 700\) K, 1–30 atm; shaded band = lean-premixed window.

phi_nox = np.linspace(0.3, 1.0, 36)
p_nox = [1, 10, 30]                     # atm
T_u_nox = 700.0                         # K

states_nox = [eq.equilibrium_states(phi_nox, T_u=T_u_nox, p=pa * ATM) for pa in p_nox]
for pa, st in zip(p_nox, states_nox):
    eq.save_states(st, f"task3_nox_{pa}atm")

T_nox = [st.T for st in states_nox]
XO_nox = [eq.mole_fractions(st, ["O"])["O"] for st in states_nox]
dNO = [eq.zeldovich_no_rate(st) for st in states_nox]

i05 = np.argmin(abs(phi_nox - 0.5))

docs.title: Answers
docs.text:
1. Why is \(T_\mathrm{eq}(Z)\) asymmetric? On a linear \(Z\) axis the drop is actually steeper toward \(Z = 0\), because \(Z_\mathrm{st} = 0.0285\) is so small. Toward \(Z = 1\) it decays slowly. With complete combustion (Burke–Schumann), the temperature rise varies linearly on each side of \(Z_\mathrm{st}\):

\[ T - T_\mathrm{mix} \propto \frac{Z}{Z_\mathrm{st}}\ (Z < Z_\mathrm{st}), \qquad T - T_\mathrm{mix} \propto \frac{1 - Z}{1 - Z_\mathrm{st}}\ (Z > Z_\mathrm{st}) \] Symbol Meaning SI unit \(T\) Burned temperature K \(T_\mathrm{mix}\) Temperature of the unburned blend at \(Z\) K \(Z\), \(Z_\mathrm{st}\) Mixture fraction, stoichiometric value –

The lean branch climbs from \(Z = 0\) to \(0.0285\), so it is steep. The rich branch spreads the fixed heat release over the extra fuel mass all the way to \(Z = 1\). Heat release is limited by the fuel on the lean side and by O\(_2\) on the rich side.

2. Does the peak shift with \(\chi_\mathrm{st}\)? Slightly richer: \(Z(T_\mathrm{max})\) goes from \(0.0317\) to \(0.0324\) as \(\chi_\mathrm{st}\) goes from 0.9 to 34 s\(^{-1}\), and to \(0.0336\) just before extinction. Higher strain lets unburned H\(_2\) leak through the reaction zone. H\(_2\) diffuses fast, so the zone where heat release balances losses moves toward the fuel side.

3. The area between \(T(Z)\) and \(T_\mathrm{eq}(Z)\) is the enthalpy not yet released as heat, because of incomplete combustion and dissociation not recombining. Its size is set by the Damköhler number \(\mathrm{Da} \sim \tau_\mathrm{mix}/\tau_\mathrm{chem} \sim 1/(\chi_\mathrm{st}\,\tau_\mathrm{chem})\): higher \(\chi_\mathrm{st}\) gives less time for chemistry and a larger gap.

4. Closest to extinction: the burning branch ends between \(a = 5000\) s\(^{-1}\) (\(\chi_\mathrm{st} \approx 81\) s\(^{-1}\), \(T_\mathrm{max} \approx 1506\) K) and \(a = 6000\) s\(^{-1}\), where the solution collapses to pure mixing. Of the main five, \(\chi_\mathrm{st} = 33.9\) s\(^{-1}\) is closest. You detect it in the flame object by flame.T.max() dropping to the inlet temperature (and the heat release, flame.heat_release_rate, going to zero). This scan restarts every solve from scratch; a strain-rate continuation from the last burning solution would pin the limit more precisely.

5. Why the lowest-strain flame still differs from equilibrium: (a) \(\chi_\mathrm{st} \approx 0.9\) s\(^{-1}\) is small but not zero, so the radicals do not fully recombine; (b) mainly differential diffusion. H\(_2\) is very light (Lewis number \(\approx 0.3\)), so it diffuses ahead of heat. The element-based \(Z\) is then no longer a conserved enthalpy coordinate, and \(T\) even exceeds \(T_\mathrm{eq}\) on the lean side (\(Z < 0.02\)). The equilibrium envelope assumes equal diffusivities.

The measured \(\chi_\mathrm{st}\) is about \(2\times\) the constant-density analytic value, and the measured maximum strain is about \(15\times\) the target \(a\). Both come from the large density difference between the H\(_2\) and air jets, which the project's equal-mass-flux formula does not account for.

docs.text:
• HRR vs T peak: heat release peaks at \(x \approx 21.03\) mm where \(T \approx 1000\) K, early in the flame. \(T\) has no interior peak: it keeps rising to \(T_b\) at the outlet. Chain branching (\(\mathrm{H + O_2 \rightarrow OH + O}\)) and fast exothermic steps peak in the reaction zone. Further downstream, slow three-body radical recombination keeps releasing heat over several mm, so the temperature lags the heat release.
  • OH and H: not co-located. H peaks at 21.19 mm, inside the reaction zone where it is produced; OH peaks 0.6 mm later at 21.80 mm, because it is removed only by slow recombination and persists into the post-flame gas.
  • Thickness vs domain: \(\delta_L = 0.33\) mm is only 0.55 % of the domain (the solver widened it from 3 to 6 cm), so the flame is very well contained.

docs.text:
• Higher \(S_L\) at \(\phi = 1\): mixture-averaged (233 vs 164 cm/s). The light species H\(_2\) and H diffuse much faster than heat (\(Le_{\mathrm{H_2}} \approx 0.3\), \(Le_\mathrm{H} \approx 0.2\)). Forcing \(D_k = \alpha\) slows the H atoms that diffuse upstream to start chain branching in the preheat zone, so the Le = 1 flame is slower.
  • Non-conserved \(Z\): \(Z\) is built from element mass fractions, so it is conserved only if all species diffuse at the same rate. Element conservation in a steady 1D flame gives
\[ \rho u\, Z_\mathrm{H} + J_\mathrm{H} = \text{const} = \rho u\, Z_{\mathrm{H},u} \quad\Rightarrow\quad Z_\mathrm{H} = Z_{\mathrm{H},u} - \frac{J_\mathrm{H}}{\rho u} \] Symbol Meaning SI unit \(\rho u\) Mass flux through the flame (constant) kg/(m²·s) \(Z_\mathrm{H}\) Mass fraction of element H – \(J_\mathrm{H}\) Diffusive mass flux of element H (sum over species) kg/(m²·s)

Wherever H-carrying species diffuse faster than the rest, \(J_\mathrm{H} \ne 0\) and \(Z\) departs from its inlet value. In this run \(Z\) does not rise in the preheat zone, as the page expects; it dips by 20 % (0.0285 → 0.0228) at the reaction zone. H\(_2\) diffuses downstream into the reaction zone, down its steep gradient (\(J_\mathrm{H} > 0\)), so less hydrogen is carried by convection there. No "extra" hydrogen accumulates; it is moved ahead by diffusion and consumed. Under Le = 1 all species diffuse together and \(Z\) stays at \(Z_\mathrm{st}\) to machine precision. - Methane: much weaker. \(Le_{\mathrm{CH_4}} \approx 0.97\), so CH\(_4\) diffuses almost exactly like heat and \(Z\) would stay nearly constant (small deviations come only from the H and H\(_2\) intermediates).

docs.text:
• \(S_L\) peak: 313 cm/s at \(\phi \approx 1.7\) (mixture-averaged), far richer than the \(T_\mathrm{ad}\) peak (\(\phi \approx 1.06\), Part 1). Rich H\(_2\) mixtures contain more of the fast-diffusing fuel and the H radical pool, which increases reactivity and diffusivity even though the flame is cooler.
  • The gap between the models: not quite as the page states. The curves cross at \(\phi \approx 0.67\). Below that, Le = 1 is faster (36 vs 16 cm/s at \(\phi = 0.4\), a factor 2.3, the largest relative gap). Above it, mixture-averaged is faster, with the largest absolute gap on the rich side (\(\approx 126\) cm/s at \(\phi = 1.6\)–1.7). Lewis-number argument: the unity-Lewis model makes H\(_2\) and H diffuse slower but heavy O\(_2\) and H\(_2\)O faster. On the rich side the light-species slowdown dominates; very lean, the deficient reactant is still H\(_2\), but the faster heat and O\(_2\) transport of the Le = 1 model wins. Planar flames are unstretched, so the thermodiffusive enhancement of lean H\(_2\) (cellular flames) does not show up here.
  • \(\delta_L\) vs \(S_L\): inversely related. The thin flames are the fast ones (\(\delta_L \sim \alpha/S_L\)), and \(\delta_L\) grows steeply on the lean side where \(S_L\) collapses. But \(S_L\delta_L\) varies a lot with \(\phi\) (124 to 951 mm²/s), because the relevant diffusivity changes with the burned temperature and composition.

docs.text:
• Exponents (mixture-averaged): \(S_L \propto p^{-0.18}\), not the \(\approx -0.5\) the page expects. \(S_L(p)\) is not a power law: its local slope steepens from \(\approx 0\) at 1 atm to \(\approx -0.5\) at 10 atm, which the dotted fit cannot follow. Under Le = 1, \(S_L\) even rises slightly up to \(\approx 3\) atm before falling (\(n = -0.03\)). Thickness is a clean power law for both models: \(\delta_L \propto p^{-1.15}\) and \(p^{-1.13}\). Preheat gives \(S_L \propto T_u^{1.69}\) (Le = 1: \(T_u^{1.60}\)), inside the typical 1.5–2.0, so H\(_2\) follows the usual trend; \(\delta_L \propto T_u^{0.43}\).
  • Why \(S_L\) falls with \(p\) and \(\delta_L\) falls faster: \(S_L \sim \sqrt{\alpha\,\omega}\) with \(\alpha \propto 1/p\). If the overall rate scaled as \(\omega \propto p\), \(S_L\) would not change; it falls because the three-body step \(\mathrm{H + O_2 + M \rightarrow HO_2 + M}\) strengthens with pressure and competes with chain branching. Meanwhile \(\delta_L \sim \alpha / S_L\) carries the full \(1/p\) of \(\alpha\), so it falls almost as \(p^{-1}\).
  • Preheat vs pressure: +200 K preheat raises \(S_L\) from 233 to 527 cm/s (+126 %); doubling \(p\) to 2 atm lowers it to 227 cm/s (−3 %). Preheat is by far the stronger lever, which is why high-inlet-temperature and recuperated combustors face flashback risk with H\(_2\), and why high pressure alone does not slow a flame much.
  • \(S_L \delta_L\): it has units of diffusivity and approximates the thermal diffusivity \(\alpha\), since \(\delta_L \sim \alpha/S_L\). It is not constant with pressure here: it drops from 767 to 36 mm²/s between 1 and 10 atm, because \(\alpha \propto 1/p\). Normalising by the unburned \(\alpha_u\) removes most of that: \(S_L\delta_L/\alpha_u\) only varies from about 8 to 17. It stays above 1 because \(\delta_L\) is set by the hot gas, where \(\alpha\) is much larger than at 300 K.

def equilibrium_temperature(phi, fuel="H2", T_u=300.0, p=101325.0,
                             mechanism="h2o2.yaml",
                             oxidizer="O2:1, N2:3.76"):
    """
    Return the adiabatic flame temperature for a single condition.

    Parameters
    ----------
    phi : float
        Equivalence ratio.
    fuel : str
        Cantera fuel string (default: "H2").
    T_u : float
        Unburned mixture temperature in K (default: 300 K).
    p : float
        Pressure in Pa (default: 1 atm).
    mechanism : str
        Cantera mechanism file (default: "h2o2.yaml").
    oxidizer : str
        Oxidizer composition string (default: "O2:1, N2:3.76").

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Adiabatic flame temperature in K.
    """
    ...

    gas = ct.Solution(mechanism)
    gas.set_equivalence_ratio(phi, fuel, oxidizer)
    gas.TP = T_u, p

    gas.equilibrate("HP")

    return gas.T

phi = 1.0
T_H2 = equilibrium_temperature(phi)

print(f"Adiabatic flame temperature for {phi} equivalence ratio: {T_H2:.2f} K")
Output
Adiabatic flame temperature for 1.0 equivalence ratio: 2387.64 K

def equilibrium_sweep(phi_range, fuel="H2", T_u=300.0, p=101325.0,
                      mechanism="h2o2.yaml", oxidizer="O2:1, N2:3.76"):
    """
    Return T_ad for an array of equivalence ratios.

    Parameters
    ----------
    phi_range : array-like
        Array of equivalence ratios.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        Adiabatic flame temperatures in K, same shape as phi_range.
    """
    ...

    phi_range = np.asarray(phi_range, dtype=float)

def equilibrium_map(phi_range, sweep_range, sweep_param="T_u",
                    fuel="H2", fixed_T_u=300.0, fixed_p=101325.0,
                    mechanism="h2o2.yaml", oxidizer="O2:1, N2:3.76"):
    """
    Compute a 2D map of T_ad over (phi, sweep_param).

    Parameters
    ----------
    phi_range : array-like
        Equivalence ratio axis.
    sweep_range : array-like
        Values of the swept parameter (T_u in K or p in Pa).
    sweep_param : {"T_u", "p"}
        Which parameter to sweep on the second axis.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray, shape (len(phi_range), len(sweep_range))
        T_ad in K at each (phi, sweep_param) point.
    """

    phi_range   = np.asarray(phi_range, dtype=float)
    sweep_range = np.asarray(sweep_range, dtype=float)
    PHI, SWEEP  = np.meshgrid(phi_range, sweep_range, indexing="ij")   # (n_phi, n_sweep)

    T_u = SWEEP if sweep_param == "T_u" else fixed_T_u
    p   = SWEEP if sweep_param == "p"   else fixed_p

    states = ct.SolutionArray(ct.Solution(mechanism), shape=PHI.shape)
    states.set_equivalence_ratio(PHI, fuel, oxidizer)
    states.TP = T_u, p
    states.equilibrate("HP")
    return states.T

def plot_equilibrium_map(phi_range, sweep_range, sweep_param="T_u", **kwargs):
    """Plot the T_ad map as a 2D contour (left) and a 3D surface (right).
    Extra keyword arguments (fuel, fixed_T_u, fixed_p, ...) go to equilibrium_map.
    Returns (fig, T_ad)."""
    phi_range   = np.asarray(phi_range, dtype=float)
    sweep_range = np.asarray(sweep_range, dtype=float)
    T_ad = equilibrium_map(phi_range, sweep_range, sweep_param, **kwargs)

    if sweep_param == "T_u":
        x, xlabel = sweep_range, "Unburned temperature $T_u$ (K)"
    else:
        x, xlabel = sweep_range / ct.one_atm, "Pressure (atm)"
    X, PHI = np.meshgrid(x, phi_range, indexing="xy")      # shape (n_phi, n_sweep), matches T_ad

    i, j = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(T_ad), T_ad.shape)   # hottest point

    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(14, 5.5))

    ax2d = fig.add_subplot(1, 2, 1)
    cs = ax2d.contourf(X, PHI, T_ad, levels=20, cmap="inferno")
    ax2d.contour(X, PHI, T_ad, levels=10, colors="k", linewidths=0.4, alpha=0.5)
    ax2d.plot(X[i, j], PHI[i, j], "c*", ms=14,
              label=f"max {T_ad[i, j]:.0f} K at $\\phi$={PHI[i, j]:.2f}")
    ax2d.set(xlabel=xlabel, ylabel="Equivalence ratio $\\phi$", title="2D map")
    ax2d.legend(loc="upper left")
    fig.colorbar(cs, ax=ax2d, label="$T_{ad}$ (K)")

    ax3d = fig.add_subplot(1, 2, 2, projection="3d")
    surf = ax3d.plot_surface(X, PHI, T_ad, cmap="inferno", edgecolor="none")
    ax3d.scatter(X[i, j], PHI[i, j], T_ad[i, j], color="cyan", s=40)
    ax3d.set(xlabel=xlabel, ylabel="$\\phi$", zlabel="$T_{ad}$ (K)", title="3D surface")
    ax3d.view_init(elev=25, azim=-130)
    fig.colorbar(surf, ax=ax3d, shrink=0.6, pad=0.1, label="$T_{ad}$ (K)")

    fig.suptitle(f"Adiabatic flame temperature, {kwargs.get('fuel', 'H2')}/air")
    plt.tight_layout()
    return fig, T_ad

def solve_counterflow(strain_rate, mechanism="h2o2.yaml",
                      fuel="H2", T_fuel=300.0, T_ox=300.0,
                      p=101325.0, width=0.02):
    """
    Solve a H2/air counterflow diffusion flame at a given strain rate.

    Parameters
    ----------
    strain_rate : float
        Target strain rate in 1/s.
    mechanism : str
        Cantera mechanism file.
    fuel : str
        Fuel species name.
    T_fuel : float
        Fuel stream temperature in K.
    T_ox : float
        Oxidiser stream temperature in K.
    p : float
        Pressure in Pa.
    width : float
        Domain width in m.

    Returns
    -------
    cantera.CounterflowDiffusionFlame
        Solved flame object.
    """
    gas = ct.Solution(mechanism)

    fuel_stream = f"{fuel}:1"
    ox_stream   = "O2:0.21, N2:0.79"

    flame = ct.CounterflowDiffusionFlame(gas, width=width)
    flame.fuel_inlet.X       = fuel_stream
    flame.fuel_inlet.T       = T_fuel
    flame.oxidizer_inlet.X   = ox_stream
    flame.oxidizer_inlet.T   = T_ox
    flame.P                  = p

    # Set mass fluxes to achieve target strain rate
    # For symmetric counterflow: a ≈ 2 * mdot / (rho * L/2)
    gas.TPX = T_fuel, p, fuel_stream
    rho_f   = gas.density
    gas.TPX = T_ox,   p, ox_stream
    rho_ox  = gas.density
    mdot    = strain_rate * 0.5 * width * 0.5 * (rho_f + rho_ox)
    flame.fuel_inlet.mdot      = mdot
    flame.oxidizer_inlet.mdot  = mdot

    flame.set_refine_criteria(ratio=3, slope=0.05, curve=0.1)
    flame.solve(loglevel=0, auto=True)

    return flame

def extract_TZ_profile(flame, fuel="H2", oxidizer="O2:1, N2:3.76"):
    """
    Extract temperature and mixture fraction profiles from a solved flame.

    Returns
    -------
    Z : numpy.ndarray
        Mixture fraction at each grid point.
    T : numpy.ndarray
        Temperature in K at each grid point.
    chi_st : float
        Scalar dissipation rate at the stoichiometric surface (1/s).
    """
    Z   = flame.mixture_fraction("Bilger")        # flame method: element or "Bilger"
    T   = flame.T

    # Z_st from a separate gas object: gas method takes (fuel, oxidizer)
    solution = ct.Solution(flame.gas.source)
    solution.set_equivalence_ratio(1.0, fuel, oxidizer)
    Z_st   = solution.mixture_fraction(fuel, oxidizer)

    # chi = 2 D (dZ/dx)^2 is not provided by Cantera, so compute it from Z(x)
    D      = flame.thermal_conductivity / (flame.density * flame.cp_mass)
    chi    = 2 * D * np.gradient(Z, flame.grid) ** 2     # χ(x), 1/s
    idx_st = np.argmin(np.abs(Z - Z_st))
    chi_st = chi[idx_st]

    return Z, T, chi_st

def equilibrium_T_of_Z(Z_range, fuel="H2", T_fuel=300.0, T_ox=300.0,
                       p=101325.0, mechanism="h2o2.yaml",
                       oxidizer="O2:0.21, N2:0.79"):
    """
    Compute the equilibrium temperature as a function of mixture fraction.

    For each Z, the mixture is the linear blend of fuel and oxidiser streams.
    The result is the upper-bound temperature envelope for any non-premixed flame.

    Parameters
    ----------
    Z_range : array-like
        Mixture fraction values in [0, 1].

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        T_eq in K at each Z.
    """
    Z_range = np.asarray(Z_range, dtype=float)
    gas     = ct.Solution(mechanism)
    T_eq    = np.zeros(len(Z_range))

    # Fuel and oxidiser streams: mass fractions and specific enthalpy
    gas.TPX = T_fuel, p, f"{fuel}:1"
    Y_fuel, h_fuel = gas.Y.copy(), gas.enthalpy_mass

    gas.TPX = T_ox, p, oxidizer
    Y_ox,   h_ox   = gas.Y.copy(), gas.enthalpy_mass

    for i, Z in enumerate(Z_range):
        Y_mix   = Z * Y_fuel + (1.0 - Z) * Y_ox
        h_mix   = Z * h_fuel + (1.0 - Z) * h_ox            # blended enthalpy
        gas.TPY = 0.5 * (T_fuel + T_ox), p, Y_mix          # sets the composition
        gas.HPY = h_mix, p, Y_mix                          # state with the blended enthalpy
        gas.equilibrate("HP")
        T_eq[i] = gas.T

    return T_eq

import cantera as ct

def solve_free_flame(phi, T_u=300.0, p=101325.0,
                     transport="mixture-averaged",
                     fuel="H2", oxidizer="O2:1, N2:3.76",
                     mechanism="h2o2.yaml", width=0.03):
    """
    Solve a freely propagating premixed flame.

    Parameters
    ----------
    phi : float
        Equivalence ratio.
    T_u : float
        Unburned mixture temperature in K.
    p : float
        Pressure in Pa.
    transport : {"mixture-averaged", "unity-Lewis-number"}
        Transport model.
    fuel : str
        Fuel species name.
    oxidizer : str
        Oxidizer composition string.
    mechanism : str
        Cantera mechanism file.
    width : float
        Domain width in m.

    Returns
    -------
    cantera.FreeFlame
        Solved flame object.
    """
    gas = ct.Solution(mechanism, transport_model=transport)
    gas.set_equivalence_ratio(phi, fuel, oxidizer)
    gas.TP = T_u, p

    flame = ct.FreeFlame(gas, width=width)
    flame.set_refine_criteria(ratio=2.0, slope=0.005, curve=0.01)
    flame.set_max_grid_points(flame.flame, 10000)
    flame.solve(loglevel=0, auto=True)

    return flame

def flame_thickness(flame):
    """
    Return the thermal flame thickness.

    float

def flame_speed_sweep(phi_range, T_u=300.0, p=101325.0,
                      transport="mixture-averaged",
                      fuel="H2", oxidizer="O2:1, N2:3.76",
                      mechanism="h2o2.yaml"):
    """
    Compute S_L over a range of equivalence ratios.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        S_L in m/s, same shape as phi_range.
    """
    phi_range = np.asarray(phi_range, dtype=float)
    S_L = np.empty_like(phi_range)

    for i, phi in np.ndenumerate(phi_range):
        flame = solve_free_flame(phi, T_u, p, transport, fuel, oxidizer, mechanism)
        S_L[i] = flame_speed(flame)

def flame_thickness_sweep(phi_range, T_u=300.0, p=101325.0,
                           transport="mixture-averaged",
                           fuel="H2", oxidizer="O2:1, N2:3.76",

    """
    Compute delta_L over a range of equivalence ratios.

        delta_L in m, same shape as phi_range.

    phi_range = np.asarray(phi_range, dtype=float)

        T = flame.T

        dTdx = np.gradient(T, x)
        delta_L[i] = float((T[-1] - T[0]) / np.max(dTdx))
